subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own a first-class `openclaw instance` Docker lifecycle, or should multi-instance Docker management stay as documented profile/port/Compose primitives plus external helpers?
rationale: Current main has the lower-level primitives to run multiple gateways, but an official lifecycle command would add new setup, update, deletion, state, and security contracts that require maintainer product direction before implementation.

options.title: Design a minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product-design anchor for create/list/delete/update commands with explicit persistence, cleanup, port, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Continue documenting named profiles, unique ports, Compose, and ClawDock-style helper commands as the supported Docker workflow.

options.title: Prove externally first
options.body: Ask for a ClawHub or standalone helper package that proves the workflow before promoting any core CLI surface.

recommendation.title: Design a minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product-design anchor for create/list/delete/update commands with explicit persistence, cleanup, port, and upgrade semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across the multi-gateway docs, CLI/container targeting, and setup product-boundary work.
